scope: Fresh text-only review of all four English prose objects and all seven final paragraphs against the actual approved Chinese lesson and actual raw lesson at the prepared paths. No visual or publishing approval.

bindingChecks.paragraphContentRedistributedWithinObjec: The source's time-pattern comparison is in Chinese final paragraph 4 and English final paragraph 5. It remains in the same source-bound prose object; neither order of concepts nor content is lost.

scientificAssessment.mechanicalElectricalAnalogy: A pendulum is not unconditionally an ideal harmonic oscillator: its restoring term is proportional to sin(theta), with the familiar linear oscillator obtained in the small-angle model. The ideal linear LC model neglects losses; unmatched damping, driving, or nonlinearity cannot be silently equated. The English explicitly limits the analogy to corresponding models and appropriate conditions and says can obey, so it does not assert equivalence of every physical oscillation.
scientificAssessment.quantityDistinction: In the standard mass-spring/LC correspondence, capacitor charge plays the mathematical role of displacement, and circuit current the role of velocity. Charge and current retain electrical dimensions and meanings. The text compares how a quantity changes with time and explicitly denies physical identity; it does not describe electromagnetic quantities as mechanical displacement.
scientificAssessment.waveClaim: Different wave kinds can share a linear wave equation and propagation relations in appropriate models. Shared mathematical form does not imply identical medium, physical quantity, speed, or arbitrary nonlinear/dispersive/dissipative behavior. The English uses can likewise share and under corresponding conditions, rather than an unconditional all-waves claim.
scientificAssessment.caveatAdequacy: The qualification is substantive, scientifically justified, and proportionate to an introduction explaining the order of study. This passage does not derive an equation or make a numerical prediction requiring a specified angle or loss threshold. It need not add those derivations or new examples to communicate the bounded analogy correctly.
scientificAssessment.notMechanicalApproval: The author's clarification claim and native PASS were not used as scientific proof. The new English wording was assessed directly, with official physics texts consulted for model limits.

blockFindings.science: The pendulum/coil-capacitor analogy is now model- and condition-limited. The time-change explanation separates electrical quantities from mechanical displacement. The wave analogy is likewise conditional. See the independently justified caveat decisions below.
blockFindings.fidelity: The swinging pendulum, capacitor discharging through a coil, mass on a spring, circuit current, comparison of temporal laws, and extension to physically different waves all remain. The source's categorical wording is intentionally qualified, not silently passed as a universal scientific truth.

blockFindings.fidelity: The field's unified viewpoint, practical importance, machine/mechanism vibrations, and both technological applications remain. Results provide a foundation accurately conveys the source's foundational role.

scientificClarificationsReviewed.englishExact: In corresponding models and under the appropriate conditions, mechanical and electromagnetic oscillations can obey the same mathematical laws.
scientificClarificationsReviewed.sourceMeaning: The raw lesson and approved Chinese state categorically that mechanical and electromagnetic oscillations completely obey the same quantitative laws.
scientificClarificationsReviewed.judgment: Accept the narrower English claim. It preserves the reason for joint study while ruling out unconditional equivalence; the pendulum small-angle and ideal LC assumptions demonstrate why the qualification matters.

scientificClarificationsReviewed.englishExact:
To see the connection, focus on how a quantity changes with time, rather than on what is oscillating, such as a mass attached to a spring or the current in a circuit.
This does not make the mechanical and electrical quantities the same physical thing.
scientificClarificationsReviewed.sourceMeaning: The raw lesson compares how oscillation proceeds rather than what oscillates, naming a spring oscillator and circuit current.
scientificClarificationsReviewed.judgment: Accept the explanatory clarification. It keeps both examples and distinguishes an abstract time-dependent quantity from the physical object and from quantities in another domain; it does not equate current with displacement.

scientificClarificationsReviewed.englishExact: Wave processes of different physical kinds can likewise share mathematical laws under corresponding conditions.
scientificClarificationsReviewed.sourceMeaning: The raw lesson and approved Chinese say that wave processes of different physical kinds all obey the same laws.
scientificClarificationsReviewed.judgment: Accept the conditional English formulation. It preserves the cross-domain motivation while avoiding a claim that every wave shares all laws regardless of model and propagation conditions.
